request: Thunderwing Gyronaut: a small gnome flyer (Flying, Ranged: hurls sparks 2 spaces). She wears a backpack with a propeller on its BACK and two mechanical bat wings; these are separate attached props that follow her spine bone, so you only animate her skeleton (the game spins the propeller and the wings are not rigged). REFERENCE VIDEO: the owner had Runway make a short video of each move. Its frames are in the folder refs/ (Read the pictures with the Read tool): refs/gyrocopter-ace--front.jpg, --side.jpg, --back.jpg are her model from 3 sides; refs/gyrocopter-ace-<clip>-<view>/frames/<move>/fNN.jpg are video frames in time order (12 evenly spaced frames per 3 s move, every other frame given, f12 = end). FIRST look at all the pictures for a move, then match her BODY and LIMB poses frame by frame: torso lean and twist, head tilt, arm and leg angles, height above the ground, and the timing (frame N of 12 = N/12 of the clip). This is a rig motion reference only. IGNORE in the video: face and mouth (never animate the face), the propeller jumping onto her head (it stays on the back of the pack), any camera drift, and the moment she spins around in the knocked-back move (she never turns her back). If refs/ is missing or empty, do NOT write any animation files (the job will be retried). Flying overrides the usual 'feet planted' rule: she hovers, her feet never touch the ground; raise her with move on the hips bone (about 12% of her height) and keep that same hover height at frame 0 and the last frame of every clip so they join up. Smooth, even game animation. This job makes OH_Hover and OH_Fly from the video clip 'fly'. All four Gyronaut clips start and end in the same HOVER pose (hips raised, legs relaxed), not the standing base pose: key the hips (and any bone you change) at frame 0 and the last frame yourself. BASE POSE (important, changed after the first try): these clips use "base_pose": "rest", so ctx.key turns are relative to the model's REST pose, which is a straight, square, front-facing A-pose (arms angled out and down from the shoulders, legs straight and parallel), the same pose as refs/gyrocopter-ace--front.jpg. The first try started from her Meshy Idle stance, which is turned to one side with crossed legs, so she did not face the camera like the video. Now she must face straight forward like the video: do not twist hips or spine. Key the arms yourself at frame 0 and the last frame into the relaxed hover pose seen in the video's first frame (upper arms hanging down and a little out from the body, elbows slightly bent).

animations.name: OH_Hover
animations.description: Hover idle, from the video clip 'fly', first move 'hover-idle' (refs/gyrocopter-ace-fly-front/frames/hover-idle and -fly-side/frames/hover-idle). She floats in place: body bobs gently up and down twice in the 3 s, knees slightly bent, feet hanging relaxed with toes down, arms loose a little away from the body, small counter-sway of arms on each bob. Loops seamlessly.

animations.name: OH_Fly
animations.description: Flying forward, from the video clip 'fly', second move 'fly-forward' (refs/.../frames/fly-forward). Used while she travels between board spaces (the game moves her; she stays on the spot). Starts from the hover pose, leans the whole body forward (cap it at about 20-25 degrees even if the video leans more), legs trail back, arms swept back along her sides, a steady rhythmic bob like wing beats, then eases back to the hover pose at the end so it loops.
